Identify hub TFs

identify_hub_TFs.Rd

Identifies hub TFs per module using values of module membership and degree. TFs with high module membership (correlation of their activity with the module score > mm_thresh, with the correlation used to build the network, corr_type of compute.WTCNA()) and a degree at or above the degree_thresh quantile of their module are considered hub TFs. The degree of a TF is its intramodular connectivity, as in WGCNA: the sum of its network adjacencies with the other TFs of the same module. The adjacencies are computed as in compute.WTCNA(), with the same soft-thresholding power, network type and correlation (for a "signed" network, \(((1 + r)/2)^{power}\), so a negative correlation adds almost nothing instead of being subtracted).

Usage

identify_hub_TFs(network, mm_thresh = 0.8, degree_thresh = 0.9)

Arguments

network

TF network obtained from compute.WTCNA().

mm_thresh

Threshold for module membership. Default is 0.8.

degree_thresh

Quantile threshold for degree within each module. Default is 0.9 (top 10%).

Value

A list with two elements:

hubGenes

Named list of hub TFs per module. Modules without hub TFs are left out (a message lists them).

detailedData

Data frame with one row per hub TF (TF names as row names) and the columns Module, ModuleMembership and Degree.

Details

The TF activities are taken from network (element TFs_matrix) and matched to the module scores by sample name. For a multi-cohort network (compute.WTCNA() with batch), the per-cohort TF activities are stacked to compute the membership, and the degree is the mean of the per-cohort degrees (each with the power of its cohort).

Networks built before the soft-thresholding power was stored in network (element Network parameters) have their power chosen again with the rule of compute.WTCNA() (with a message), assuming a signed network and Pearson correlation.

Examples


data("network.tuto")

hub_tfs <- identify_hub_TFs(network.tuto, mm_thresh = 0.8, degree_thresh = 0.9)
